title: Reported speech 2
note: b1_reported_speech already carries statements, backshift, said/told and if/wh. This unit is the two things it does not drill: the WORD ORDER of a reported question (*He asked me where did I live) and ask/tell + object + to-infinitive for commands and requests. Backshift itself is recycled, not re-taught (F1). Thickened 10 -> 25 items 2026-09-04 (agent loop): 15 new - wh- questions across where/what/when/why/how/who/what time, yes-no with if and the whether card 2 promises, ask/tell + object + to, and both negative commands (not to). Rules applied this pass: A8 twin closed on the had-arrived items; A4 both cleared (the station -> my bag, The teacher -> Our teacher, plus Czech demonstratives where the noun really is definite); F3 `earlier` swapped for `at six`. C4: the whether promised on card 2 now has an item, instead of a card promising a form the bank never drills. B4/B6: every option list carries this unit's own errors - did-inversion, aux-inversion, said + person, and the bare verb after ask/tell. · C57 recap card (You already know — Nepřímá řeč 1) added as card 1.

cards.title: Reported questions and commands
points: A reported question is no longer a question. It takes statement order.

cards.title: You already know
points: After past **said** / **told**, the verb steps back one tense — **backshift**.
You can leave **that** out: *He said (that) he was tired.*
Reported speech 1 did **statements**. Here it is questions and commands.

cards.title: No did, no inversion
points: The subject comes **before** the verb, exactly as in a normal sentence.

cards.title: Commands and requests
points: Both verbs need a person after them: told **me**, asked **me**.

cards.title: Common mistakes
points: A reported question uses statement order, and **tell /** ask need a person.

rows: ~~He asked me where did I live.~~
~~She asked me what am I doing.~~
She asked me what **I was** doing.

items.en: He asked me where I lived.
items.cz: Zeptal se mě, kde bydlím.
items.gap: He asked me where ____. (I / live)
accepts: He asked me where I lived.
items.wrong: He asked me where did I live.
items.explanation: Statement order after **where**: subject **I** then the verb **lived**. No did.
items.explanation_cz: Po **where** je pořádek jako ve větě oznamovací: podmět **I**, pak sloveso **lived**. Žádné did.

items.en: She asked if I wanted coffee.
items.cz: Zeptala se, jestli chci kávu.
items.gap: She asked ____ I wanted coffee. (if / what)
accepts: She asked if I wanted coffee.
items.explanation: The direct question had no question word, so it takes **if**.
items.explanation_cz: Přímá otázka neměla tázací slovo, takže se použije **if**.

items.en: He told me to wait outside.
items.cz: Řekl mi, abych čekal venku.
items.gap: He told me ____ outside. (wait)
accepts: He told me to wait outside.
items.wrong: He said me to wait outside.
items.explanation: **tell** + me + **to wait**. The to-infinitive carries the command.
items.explanation_cz: **tell** + me + **to wait**. Příkaz nese infinitiv s to.

items.en: She asked me what I was doing.
items.cz: Zeptala se mě, co dělám.
items.gap: She asked me what ____. (I / do)
accepts: She asked me what I was doing.
items.wrong: She asked me what was I doing.
items.explanation: Statement order after **what**: I was doing.
items.explanation_cz: Po **what** pořádek oznamovací věty: I was doing.

items.en: She asked me to help her.
items.cz: Poprosila mě, abych jí pomohl.
items.gap: She asked me ____ her. (help)
accepts: She asked me to help her.
items.wrong: She asked me help her.
items.explanation: **ask** + me + **to help**. A request takes the same pattern as a command.
items.explanation_cz: **ask** + me + **to help**. Prosba má stejný vzorec jako příkaz.

items.en: He told me not to worry.
items.cz: Řekl mi, ať se nebojím.
items.gap: He told me ____ worry. (not)
accepts: He told me not to worry.
items.wrong: He told me don't worry.
items.explanation: Negative command: **not to** + the plain verb.
items.explanation_cz: Záporný příkaz: **not to** + základní tvar slovesa.

items.en: I asked her where my bag was.
items.cz: Zeptal jsem se jí, kde mám tašku.
items.gap: I asked her where ____. (my bag / be)
accepts: I asked her where my bag was.
items.wrong: I asked her where was my bag.
items.explanation: Statement order after **where**: the noun first, then the verb — **my bag was**.
items.explanation_cz: Po **where** je pořádek jako v oznamovací větě: nejdřív podstatné jméno, pak sloveso — **my bag was**.

items.en: They asked if we could come at six.
items.cz: Zeptali se, jestli můžeme přijít v šest.
items.gap: They asked ____ we could come at six. (if / that)
accepts: They asked if we could come at six.
items.explanation: No question word in the original, so **if**. *can* has moved back to **could**.
items.explanation_cz: V původní otázce nebylo tázací slovo, takže **if**. *can* se posunulo na **could**.
items.wrong: They asked did we could come at six.

items.en: Our teacher told us to open our books.
items.cz: Náš učitel nám řekl, ať si otevřeme knihy.
items.gap: Our teacher told us ____ our books. (open)
accepts: Our teacher told us to open our books.
items.wrong: Our teacher said us to open our books.
items.explanation: **tell** + us + **to open**.
items.explanation_cz: **tell** + us + **to open**.

items.en: He asked me when I had arrived.
items.cz: Zeptal se mě, kdy jsem přijel.
items.gap: He asked me when ____. (I / arrive)
accepts: He asked me when I had arrived.
He asked me when I'd arrived.
items.wrong: He asked me when did I arrive.
items.explanation: Statement order, and the past simple has moved back to **had arrived**.
items.explanation_cz: Pořádek oznamovací věty a minulý čas se posunul na **had arrived**.

items.en: She asked me why I was late.
items.cz: Zeptala se mě, proč jdu pozdě.
items.gap: She asked me why ____. (I / be)
accepts: She asked me why I was late.
items.wrong: She asked me why was I late.
items.explanation: After **why** the subject comes first: why **I was**. A reported question is not a question.
items.explanation_cz: Po **why** stojí nejdřív podmět: why **I was**. Nepřímá otázka není otázka.

items.en: He asked us how we had found the flat.
items.cz: Zeptal se nás, jak jsme ten byt našli.
items.gap: He asked us how ____ the flat. (we / find)
accepts: He asked us how we had found the flat.
He asked us how we'd found the flat.
items.wrong: He asked us how did we find the flat.
items.explanation: No **did** in a reported question, and the subject leads: how **we had found**.
items.explanation_cz: V nepřímé otázce není **did** a vede podmět: how **we had found**.

items.en: I asked him who had called.
items.cz: Zeptal jsem se ho, kdo volal.
items.gap: I asked him who ____. (call)
accepts: I asked him who had called.
items.wrong: I asked him who did call.
items.explanation: When **who** is the subject there is nothing to invert — just **had called**.
items.explanation_cz: Když je **who** podmět, není co obracet — prostě **had called**.

items.en: She asked me when the film started.
items.cz: Zeptala se mě, kdy ten film začíná.
items.gap: She asked me when ____. (the film / start)
accepts: She asked me when the film started.
items.wrong: She asked me when did the film start.
items.explanation: Statement order after **when**: **the film started**, with no did.
items.explanation_cz: Po **when** je pořádek oznamovací věty: **the film started**, bez did.

items.en: He asked me if I had seen the film.
items.cz: Zeptal se mě, jestli jsem ten film viděl.
items.gap: He asked me ____ I had seen the film. (if / that)
accepts: He asked me if I had seen the film.
He asked me if I'd seen the film.
items.wrong: He asked me did I see the film.
items.explanation: A yes/no question is reported with **if**, and the tense steps back to *had seen*.
items.explanation_cz: Zjišťovací otázka se převypráví s **if** a čas jde o krok zpět na *had seen*.

items.en: She asked whether I wanted to come.
items.cz: Zeptala se, jestli chci přijít.
items.gap: She asked ____ I wanted to come. (whether / that)
accepts: She asked whether I wanted to come.
She asked if I wanted to come.
items.wrong: She asked whether did I want to come.
items.explanation: **whether** is the slightly more formal twin of **if** — same job, same order after it.
items.explanation_cz: **whether** je o něco formálnější dvojče **if** — stejná práce, stejný pořádek za ním.

items.en: He asked me what my name was.
items.cz: Zeptal se mě, jak se jmenuju.
items.gap: He asked me what ____. (my name / be)
accepts: He asked me what my name was.
items.wrong: He asked me what was my name.
items.explanation: The noun goes before the verb: what **my name was**.
items.explanation_cz: Podstatné jméno stojí před slovesem: what **my name was**.

items.en: She asked me if I could drive.
items.cz: Zeptala se mě, jestli umím řídit.
items.gap: She asked me ____ I could drive. (if / what)
accepts: She asked me if I could drive.
items.wrong: She asked me could I drive.
items.explanation: *Can you drive?* is reported with **if** and no inversion: if I **could** drive.
items.explanation_cz: *Can you drive?* se převypráví s **if** a bez inverze: if I **could** drive.

items.en: He asked me where I had been.
items.cz: Zeptal se mě, kde jsem byl.
items.gap: He asked me where ____. (I / be)
accepts: He asked me where I had been.
He asked me where I'd been.
items.wrong: He asked me where had I been.
items.explanation: Subject first, then the verb: where **I had been**.
items.explanation_cz: Nejdřív podmět, pak sloveso: where **I had been**.

items.en: My boss asked me to work on Saturday.
items.cz: Šéf mě požádal, abych pracoval v sobotu.
items.gap: My boss asked me ____ on Saturday. (work)
accepts: My boss asked me to work on Saturday.
items.wrong: My boss asked me work on Saturday.
items.explanation: **ask** + a person + **to** + verb: asked me **to work**.
items.explanation_cz: **ask** + osoba + **to** + sloveso: asked me **to work**.

items.en: She told her children to be quiet.
items.cz: Řekla svým dětem, ať jsou zticha.
items.gap: She told her children ____ quiet. (be)
accepts: She told her children to be quiet.
items.wrong: She said her children to be quiet.
items.explanation: **tell** needs a person and then **to**: told her children **to be**. *say* cannot take the person like this.
items.explanation_cz: **tell** potřebuje osobu a pak **to**: told her children **to be**. *say* takhle osobu vzít nemůže.

items.en: She told me not to wait for her.
items.cz: Řekla mi, ať na ni nečekám.
items.gap: She told me ____ wait for her. (not)
accepts: She told me not to wait for her.
items.wrong: She told me don't wait for her.
items.explanation: The negative command is **not to** + verb, never *don't* inside the report.
items.explanation_cz: Záporný příkaz je **not to** + sloveso, nikdy *don't* uvnitř nepřímé řeči.

items.en: I asked them not to make so much noise.
items.cz: Poprosil jsem je, ať nedělají takový hluk.
items.gap: I asked them ____ make so much noise. (not)
accepts: I asked them not to make so much noise.
items.wrong: I asked them don't make so much noise.
items.explanation: Same shape with **ask**: asked them **not to** make.
items.explanation_cz: Stejný tvar i s **ask**: asked them **not to** make.

items.en: They told us to come back at two.
items.cz: Řekli nám, ať se vrátíme ve dvě.
items.gap: They told us ____ back at two. (come)
accepts: They told us to come back at two.
items.wrong: They said us to come back at two.
items.explanation: **told** takes the person directly; *said* would need **to us**.
items.explanation_cz: **told** bere osobu přímo; *said* by potřebovalo **to us**.

items.en: I asked her what time the train left.
items.cz: Zeptal jsem se jí, v kolik ten vlak jede.
items.gap: I asked her what time ____. (the train / leave)
accepts: I asked her what time the train left.
items.wrong: I asked her what time did the train leave.
items.explanation: **what time** behaves like any question word: the noun, then the verb.
items.explanation_cz: **what time** se chová jako každé tázací slovo: nejdřív podstatné jméno, pak sloveso.
